an0291.user: Running YouTube ads for my kids-coding edtech and I'm confused. Last 30 days I pulled 870K impressions and about 7,557 clicks, so CTR is around 0.9%. But out of all those clicks only 77 people actually bought — that's a 1.02% conversion rate. AOV is ₹1,800. I'm on broad-match keywords. Is my CTR too low? Should I change the thumbnails?
an0291.assistant:
Your CTR isn't your problem — 0.9% on YouTube broad reach is fine, and chasing it with new thumbnails will just buy you more of the wrong people. Look one step down. 7,557 clicks turned into 77 orders, a 1.02% conversion rate. That's the number screaming at you.

Here's what's happening: broad-match keywords are pouring in huge, cheap, low-intent traffic. 870K impressions sounds great, but you're reaching parents who are browsing, half-curious, not parents actively looking to enrol a child in a coding class. They click because the hook is good, then bounce because they were never in buying mode. High clicks, near-zero intent.

So stop optimising for clicks. The lever is intent: tighten your keywords to high-intent ones ("coding classes for kids", "online coding course age 8"), pile on negative keywords to cut the junk searches, and let your targeting filter for parents who are shopping, not scrolling. You'll get fewer clicks and a far better conversion rate — which is the only number that pays you.

One caveat: 77 orders is a smallish base, so once you tighten, give it 2-3 weeks before you judge the new conversion rate. Don't react to the first few days.

That pattern — strong intent all the way to checkout, then collapse — is classic last-step friction, not an acquisition problem. The usual suspects: surprise shipping cost revealed at the end, forced account creation, or missing payment options (no UPI, no COD) on an audience that expects both. People don't abandon a cart they fought to fill unless something blocks them at the till.

The lever: instrument the checkout. Add step-level analytics or a session-recording tool on those 1,380 sessions and find the exact field or screen where they drop. Don't touch the ad budget — Pmax is feeding you fine.

Caveat: confirm the 366 number isn't an attribution lag (some purchases credit late) before you assume the full gap is friction — but even allowing for that, a 27% checkout conversion has real money leaking out of it.
